name: Atul Ltd
_note: Company fact base for the GAM initiation (as of 30-Sep-2026, Q1FY27 basis). Every number carries src and published. Consolidated unless stated. Later facts are kept out (see updates/later-facts.json).

profile.what: Diversified, integrated Indian chemical company of the Lalbhai group (Ahmedabad). Incorporated 5-Sep-1947 by Kasturbhai Lalbhai; manufacturing began 17-Mar-1952 at Atul (Valsad, Gujarat), the first site in India inaugurated by Prime Minister Nehru. ~1,300-acre integrated site with 73 MW captive power and 32 MLD effluent treatment; 8 production sites; 900+ products and 400 formulations; 142 brands; ~4,000 customers in 32 industries and 88 countries.
profile.segments: Two reported segments plus a small 'Others': Life Science Chemicals (LSC: crop protection bulk actives such as 2,4-D, indoxacarb and sulfonylurea herbicides; crop protection retail brands; APIs and intermediates incl. Atul Bioscience) and Performance & Other Chemicals (P&OC: aromatics such as para-cresol and anisole derivatives, bulk chemicals incl. resorcinol, caustic-chlorine and sulphuric acid, colours (textile dyes, pigments), Polymers - Performance Materials (epoxy resins, curing agents, sulfones) and Polymers - Retail (Lapox, Polygrip adhesives)). Others = agri-biotech (tissue-culture date palms), services.
profile.src: Analyst Meet 2026 (slides 5-10); AR 2025-26 letter to shareholders

q1fy27.oci: Total comprehensive income ₹375 cr vs PAT ₹254 cr: ~₹121 cr of fair-value gains on equity investments (FVOCI) in the quarter
q1fy27.drivers: P&OC revenue +34% and EBIT 2.4x; LSC revenue +4%. Brokers attribute the margin jump partly to inventory gains and a spike in domestic chemical spreads during the West Asia conflict (ICICI Securities: 'unlikely to sustain'); cost of materials +39%, inventory drawdown ₹188 cr.

q1fy27.noCall: Atul does not host quarterly earnings calls; it publishes an investor presentation and holds an annual analyst meet (30-Apr-2026) and site visits.

guidance.value: ₹1,100 cr of sales yet to be realised from existing capacity and ₹600 cr from new projects

existing capacities 'must deliver additional consolidated sales of ₹436 cr'; own expansions 'clarity of additional sales of ₹395 cr'; retail +₹121 cr (long-term aim: retail larger than current B2B sales); JVs 'to start with ₹40 cr'
FY26 consolidated sales and PBT were the highest ever, but EBITDA margin (20% incl. other income) and ROCE (17%) remain below the 27% (FY21) and 35% (FY20) peaks

Five mandates: manufacturing/R&D excellence, digitalisation incl. AI, people productivity and lean fixed costs, conserve cash (measure performance by free cash flow), work closely with customers; build, acquire or collaborate
Focus on sweating existing assets, open to inorganic opportunities, evaluating large investments; near-term geopolitical tensions could weigh on margins

history.event: Manufacturing starts at Atul, Valsad (17-Mar-1952); site inaugurated by PM Jawaharlal Nehru
history.impact: First of India's chemical 'firsts' (vat dyes, 2,4-D, para-cresol, phosgene)

history.event: JVs with ICI (Atic, dyes), American Cyanamid (Cyanamid India, agchem/pharma) and Ciba-Geigy (Cibatul, resins); all ended by 1999
history.impact: Technology base for dyes, agchem and epoxy

history.event: JVs: Atul Rajasthan Date Palms (74:26 with Govt of Rajasthan, 2010), Rudolf Atul Chemicals (50:50, 2011), Anaven LLP with Nouryon (50:50 MCA plant, 2017)
history.impact: Anaven has run below capacity: loss ₹51 cr (FY24), PBT −₹36 cr (FY26); ₹12 cr of its loan and ₹3 cr interest overdue at Mar-26

history.event: Peak returns: ROCE 35% (FY20), EBITDA margin 27% incl. other income (FY21); first open-market buyback (₹50 cr, 2020-21)
Fire at the Atul site (20-Apr-2022); second buyback ₹70 cr (73,296 shares at an average ₹9,536, Apr-May 2022)
history.impact: Insurance claim income ₹37 cr booked in FY25

history.event: Capex peak (₹1,970 cr over three years): LER, caustic-chlorine (Atul Products), API plants
history.impact: P&OC capital employed up from ₹1,818 cr (FY22) to ₹2,747 cr (FY24) while P&OC EBIT fell from ₹576 cr to ₹240 cr

history.event: Agchem destocking and Chinese dumping: revenue −13%, EPS ₹110 (−37%); Atul Products' caustic plant starts (Dec-2023); third buyback ₹50 cr (72,000 shares at ₹6,935, Nov-2023 to Jan-2024)
history.impact: Trough year; LSC EBIT halved to ₹203 cr

history.event: Recovery: revenue +18%, EPS ₹164; LER +50 ktpa (Oct-2024); US anti-dumping duty on Indian epoxy (Atul 12.69%, Mar-2025)
Record sales (₹6,274 cr) and PBT (₹901 cr); EPS ₹230; India's anti-dumping duty on epoxy imports (Nov-2025); Atul-Buckman JV
history.impact: FCF ₹851 cr as capex fell to ₹175 cr

history.event: Record quarter: revenue +25%, EBITDA margin 21%, EPS ₹83 (+92%) on war-time chemical prices and inventory gains; ₹167 cr herbicide project approved

corporateActions: Three open-market buybacks totalling ₹170 cr (₹50 cr in 2020-21, ₹70 cr in Apr-May 2022, ₹50 cr in Nov-2023 to Jan-2024) cut the share count from ~2.966 cr to 2.944 cr. Dividend ₹30 a share on FY26 (₹25 on FY25, ₹20 on FY24). Share capital has only fallen since FY15 (no bonus, split or equity raise in FY15-26).

governance.subsidiaries: 35+ Indian subsidiaries, many dormant shells with ₹0.1 cr of net assets (e.g. Atul Paints, Atul Entertainment, Atul Hospitality, Atul Seeds), plus finance subsidiaries (Atul Finserv, Atul Fin Resources) holding investments; 50% stake in a hospital (Valsad Institute of Medical Sciences, loss ₹11 cr in FY26).
